This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation .
2.

The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 06.05.2019 at about 12.15 while moving in a lorry bearing Reg.No.KA415886 as a coolie to load SCCH 5 tree logs near Dumagere cross,
Shanthigrama Hobli, Hassan district, driver of the said lorry has driven the lorry in high speed rash and negligently, endangering to human life and turtled down loosing control over the lorry and caused the accident, out of this accident, petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately he was shifted to Sparsha Hospital through 108 ambulance, wherein he has taken conservative treatment, then he was referred to Adichunchanagiri Hospital, wherein he has taken treatment as indoor patient since 08.05.2019 to 20.06.2019, surgery is conducted, then he has taken follow up treatment, now he is under complete rest and taking follow up treatment, for all he has spent an amount of Rs.2,50,000/, out of this accident he has lost his working capacity and income.
SCCH 5 3.
Prior to the accident, he was aged about 32 years, hale and healthy, working as coolie and earning Rs.20,000/ p.m., thereby maintaining his family, but now he is unable to do anything.
Out of this accident, crime No.38/2019 is registered against the driver of the said lorry before Shanthigrama Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC.
R1 is the owner, R2 is insurer of the said lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ with interest.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has not appeared, hence placed exparte.

R2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner, further statd that very petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts, he is entitled to SCCH 5 take shelter under Sec.147 and 149 of M.V.Act, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) of M.V.Act by the R1, there is no compliance of Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act by the concerned police, driver of the lorry had no effective driving license at the time of accident, R1 has to comply the policy conditions, he has issued policy in favour of lorry bearing Reg.No.KA415886 and he is liable to pay compensation subject to compliance of policy conditions, rest of the allegations made by the petitioner is false and baseless,
there is no negligency of the lorry driver, claim made by the petitioner is higher side, petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable, so that, prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this court has framed the following:
Sri. Krishnappa vs Sri. Nagaraju on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146297657/
2 SCCH 5 ::ISSUES::
1.Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 06.05.2019 at about 12.15 p.m. near Dumagere Cross, Shanthigrama Hobli, Hassan due to rash and negligent driving of lorry bearing Reg.No.KA41 5886 by its driver, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW1, examined 1 witness as PW2 and marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, R2 has deposed his evidence as RW1 and marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 and closed his evidence.
SCCH 5 7.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1: As per story of the petitioner very accident is occurred due to negligency of driver of the lorry, owner of the lorry/R1 has placed exparte and not contested the petition, R2/insurer has contested and taken contention that, there is no negligency of the lorry driver.
In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW1, in his chiefexamination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.

In this SCCH 5 regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1.
copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.9, copy of Charge Sheet is marked as Ex.P.10.
9.

In crossexamination there is no question by the counsel for R2 about place, date and time of the accident, further there is no question that, there is no negligency of driver of the lorry, there is a question that very petitioner was not working as coolie in the said lorry and very document is Sri. Krishnappa vs Sri. Nagaraju on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146297657/
3 created.
10. On the other hand, R2 has deposed his evidence as RW1 and furnished authorization letter marked as Ex.R.1 and copy of policy marked as Ex.R.2.
In crossexamination admits that, due to negligency of the lorry driver, very accident is occurred, charge sheet is against the said lorry and its driver.
SCCH 5 11.

On going through the evidence of both the parties it is noticed that, very accident is occurred on 06.05.2019 at about 12.15 p.m. near Dumagere cross, Shanthigrama Hobli, Hassan, further it is noticed that Ex.P.10 is charge sheet in crime No.38/2019 of Shanthigrama police it is clear that,
driver of the lorry by name Yellappa had been driving the said lorry rash and negligently and caused this accident.

Further it is clear that, petitioner was worker in the said lorry and he is cited as CW6 in the said charge sheet and charge sheet is filed for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
Further in crossexamination RW1 admitted that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the lorry driver.

Under such circumstances, considering all these aspects this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, very accident is occurred due to SCCH 5 nelgiency of the lorry driver,
petitioner was working as coolie, out of this accident he sustained grievous injuries and taken treatment at Sparsh Hospital and Adichunchagiri Hospital, so that, considering the same I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained left anterior column acetabular fracture with communited minimally displaced fracture of the right superior and inferior pubic ramus.

In this regard he has furnished discharge summary marked as Ex.P.7, discharge clearance certificate marked as Ex.P.8, outpatient record marked as Ex.P.11.
13.

Further Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS Hospital has been examined as PW2 and furnished clinical notes marked as Ex.P.12, recent Xray SCCH 5 Films marked as Ex.P.13 and he has assessed total disability of the left lower limb at the rate of 42% and whole body disability at the rate of 15%.
14.
In crossexamination by counsel for R2 admits that, petitioner is not under any medicare and he can walk without any support, he is advised for mobilization of limbs after discharge.

Petitioner sustained injury on 06.05.2019, difficulties to the petitioner are mentioned on the basis of information given by him, petitioner needs regular follow up treatment, he has not issued medical certificate, he do not know the avocation of the petitioner, he denied that petitioner can do all his day to day activities without any difficulties.

15. In crossexamination PW1 admits that, he has not taken any follow up treatment, now he is ok,
after treatment at Sparsh Hospital he has taken treatment at SCCH 5 Adichunchanagiri Hospital.
Further denied that, bills are created.

On perusal of Ex.P.7 discharge summary it is noticed that,
petitioner has taken treatment at Adichunchanagiri Hospital since 08.05.2019 to 20.06.2019 wherein surgery is conducted on left lower limb, further Ex.P.8 is discharge clearance certificate Sri. Krishnappa vs Sri. Nagaraju on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146297657/
4 issued by the Sparsh Hospital which does not speaks about conduct of the surgery, Petitioner is agricultural coolie, said fact is not in dispute, further it is noticed that, with some difficulties he can walk, under such circumstances, this tribunal is of the opinion that, disability assessed by the Doctor at the rate of 42% is proper and correct, whole body disability is considered at the rate of 15%, but looking to the oral and documentary evidence, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to consider the disability at the rate of SCCH 5 13%, which will be proper and correct for the purpos of calculation of loss of future income.

16. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 32 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.3, accordingly he is born in the year 1983 and the alleged accident is occurred on 2019, accordingly relying on Ex.P.3 his age is considered about 36 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 15 is applicable with reference to Sarla Verma case.
17. As per his case, he was working as coolie and also doing agricultural operation and earning Rs.20,000/ p.m., to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal SCCH 5 Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,000/ p.m.

Keeping in mind injuries caused to the petitioner, treatment taken, expenses incurred and also the pain suffered, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to allot compensation under other heads, accordingly for pain and sufferings compensation of Rs.15,000/
is awarded, for conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges Rs.15,000/ is awarded, for loss of amenities of life Rs.15,000/ is awarded, further he is entitled for Rs.14,000/ towards loss of income during laid up period.

Further petitioner is also entitled for compensation for medical expenses SCCH 5 incurred by him, for which, he has produced medical bills marked as Ex.P.5 for an amount of Rs.51,285/ and medical bills marked as Ex.P.6 for an amount of Rs.56,200/, totally a sum of Rs.1,07,485/.
Further petitioner is also entitled for Rs.20,000/ towards future medical expenses.
19. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:
Sl. No.
Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of future income 3,27,60000 2.
Pain and sufferings 15,00000 3.
Conveyance, nourishment and 15,00000 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 1,07,48500 5.
Loss of amenities in life 15,00000

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,14,085/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/) from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

21. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.VGC0402646000103, which is valid for the period from 17.03.2019 to 16.03.2020, the alleged accident was occurred on 06.05.2019, it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Further driver of the lorry by name Yallappa had driving licence at the time of the accident,
copy of the same is on record, hence naturally liability of R1 shall go against R2, so that, R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from SCCH 5 the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

22. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,14,085/ (Rupees Five Lakhs Fourteen Thousand Eighty Five Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/) from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through epayment directly to SCCH 5 his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
